newsitem.title: CHINA: China's farmers earn, spend more.
newsitem.headline: China's farmers earn, spend more.

text.p: The per capita cash income and spending of China's farmers rose by 10.2 percent and 16.6 percent in the first nine months of 1996 compared with the year-ago period, the Xinhua news agency said in an overnight report.

The per capita cash income of Chinese farmers rose to 1,348 yuan in the first three quarters, up by 10.2 percent, or 223.70 yuan ($26.95), in real terms, Xinhua quoted the State Statistical Bureau as saying.
The per capita living expenditure of farmers topped 788 yuan, or an actual increase of 164 yuan over the same 1995 period, the largest increase so far in the 1990s, Xinhua said.
Each farmer spent an average of 312 yuan on food, an increase of 26.4 percent over the same 1995 period, and 128 yuan on accommodation, a year-on-year increase of 27 percent, the agency said.
Farmers also spent more on medical care, transportation, communications, cultural activities and education, it said without giving further details.
